key_insight: Synthetic biomedical data can accelerate model development, but its value depends on closing the simulation-to-reality gap. The paper argues that synthetic performance should be interpreted carefully because strong results in virtual experiments do not always translate to real-world clinical settings.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between performance on synthetic datasets and performance on real biomedical data, which can mislead model development and evaluation.
method: Reviews how synthetic datasets are created and used for biomedical machine learning.
Analyzes the simulation-to-reality gap as the core limitation of synthetic evaluation.
Discusses strategies for using synthetic data more reliably to gain biomedical insight and support model development.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper is a reminder that synthetic data is useful for experimentation, benchmarking, and privacy-preserving development, but real-world validation remains essential. It helps guide better dataset design, evaluation practices, and expectations about generalization.
visual_elements: Split-screen diagram comparing synthetic experiments vs. real-world deployment
Pipeline graphic showing data generation, model training, and validation
Gap illustration highlighting the simulation-to-reality mismatch
Icon set for privacy, benchmarking, and clinical translation
paper_title: From virtual experiments to biomedical insight with synthetic data
paper_authors: Margarida Victoriano, Milena Pavlović, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Hélder P. Oliveira, Artur Rocha
